plan: Given my value of $10, I should bid less than this to ensure a positive profit if I win. Rational bidders will not bid above their value, and ties are resolved randomly. A bid slightly below $10 maximizes my chance of winning while ensuring potential profit. I'll bid $9.9 to undercut any bidder with a similar value and maximize my chance of winning against those with lower values.

Given the rationality assumption, each bidder will bid slightly below their true value to maximize profit without overbidding. My value is $30. To maximize profit, I should bid slightly below $30, considering the risk of losing to a higher bid. A bid around $29.9 balances the risk of overpaying with the chance of winning the auction.

Given my value of $25 for the prize, I should bid slightly less than my value to maximize profit while still having a competitive chance to win. A bid of $24.9 ensures that if I win, my profit is positive ($25 - $24.9 = $0.1). Since all bidders are rational, they will also bid close to their values. Bidding slightly below my value is optimal to balance winning chances and profit.
